title: Propose or decide a Todo desired-state design
summary: Create, correct, inspect, accept, or reject a desired-state design for a todo whose latest situation assessment is ready.
use_when: An established todo has a latest current ready `aN` and needs a normative desired-state reconciliation.
A ready, rejected, or abandoned design needs provenance-bearing correction or explicit decision.
do_not_use_when: The current situation is unknown, stale, inconclusive, or still needs a material user choice.
The requested artifact is a task list, sequence, estimate, file edit, command, deployment, or implementation record.
The owning umbrella is completed, superseded, or otherwise not open and canonical.
outcome: One basis-complete `dN` proposal or durable return for more assessment, followed only when explicitly requested by a deterministic provenance-bearing accept or reject decision.
effects: Propose and correct submit constrained Nucleus jobs and may consume Codex allowance.
A proposal records desired ownership, boundaries, state, interfaces, lifecycle, failure, compatibility, acceptance, non-goals, and jurisdiction transitions against one exact assessment.
Correction preserves the named predecessor and feedback and creates a successor rather than editing history.
Accept/reject bypasses Nucleus and records an explicit decision with readable UTF-8 provenance.
authority: Todo owns assessment selection, design grammar, basis validation, draft lifecycle, decisions, currentness, and domain success.
The liaison may propose or return for assessment but cannot accept, reject, plan, or execute implementation.
success: A ready design has no active choices, includes all nine clause kinds, covers every direction boundary, and covers every active predecessor operation.
Correction creates a traceable successor and leaves the predecessor unchanged.
Acceptance succeeds only while the exact assessment and umbrella bases remain current and stores the decision-source path.
failure_and_recovery: When evidence is insufficient or stale, the liaison records a durable assessment return instead of inventing desired state.
A run ending with an open draft marks it abandoned; inspect and correct it explicitly rather than treating it as ready.
A newer assessment blocks acceptance and correction against the older basis; reassess and reconcile again.
privacy: Designs and assessments may contain detailed current state, ownership, constraints, and desired interfaces.
Nucleus output retains model-side source and proposal traffic; decision sources are stored by canonical path in Todo.
does_not_authorize: Implementation planning, task creation, file edits, deployment, or execution.
Design acceptance based on model prose or job completion.
Using a stale assessment or changing external-system ownership without explicit accepted desired state.

consumers.statement: A caller with an established open Todo and a current ready assessment may obtain, correct, inspect, or explicitly decide a normative desired-state design.
Implementation planners, task runners, deployment systems, and callers seeking current-state research are outside this capability.

preconditions.statement: Proposal requires an open canonical tN whose newest assessment is current and ready; correction requires an eligible ready, rejected, or abandoned dN bound to an assessment that remains current and ready.
Accept or reject requires a readable UTF-8 authorization source, and acceptance additionally requires the exact design and all recorded umbrella bases to remain current.

inputs.statement: Public inputs are an exact tN for proposal, an exact dN plus nonblank feedback for correction, or an exact dN plus decision provenance and any required rejection reason for decision.
The liaison receives only the resolved direction, exact aN, accepted predecessor if any, correction feedback if any, and a closed basis catalog; quality and exact model overrides are optional.
Arbitrary external research, free-form basis references, implementation tasks, commands, sequences, estimates, and deployment actions are rejected inputs.

outputs.statement: A successful reconciliation returns one dN with explicit jurisdiction changes, nine clause kinds, basis references, choices, predecessor or correction provenance, and open, ready, abandoned, rejected, or accepted history as applicable.
When the assessment cannot support design, the run records a separate immutable assessment return with exact aN, reason, and missing-or-stale references, allocating no dN before initial submission.

data_semantics.statement: Design is normative desired state rather than observed state or implementation; ready is structural readiness for a user decision, and accepted records authorization without planning or performing work.
Jurisdiction actions are keep, move, add, or retire, and active clauses cover ownership, boundary, state, interface, lifecycle, failure, compatibility, acceptance, and non-goal.

identity_and_units.statement: dN identifies one immutable basis-bound design history; aN identifies its exact assessment basis, while stable operation IDs and draft versions coordinate correction and revision.
This capability publishes no implementation effort, schedule, cost, or accounting unit.

completeness_and_freshness.statement: A ready design has no active choices, includes all nine clause kinds, and collectively covers the direction body, every structured direction boundary, and every active predecessor operation.
Proposal, correction, and acceptance bind and recheck one exact current assessment and exact umbrella bases; a newer assessment blocks correction and acceptance against the older basis.
Design completeness does not establish current external facts, implementation completeness, deployment readiness, or execution success.

access.statement: The current-user Todo CLI uses a constrained Nucleus liaison for propose or correct and deterministic direct Todo writes for accept or reject.
The liaison has no external research, shell, workspace, web, implementation, deployment, design-decision, or routing-decision interface.

lifecycle_and_consistency.statement: Initial design submission validates atomically before allocating dN; correction records immutable feedback and creates a successor rather than editing its predecessor.

Open drafts left by a completed run become abandoned, assessment returns are terminal for their run, and accept or reject commits a deterministic provenance-bearing decision after current-basis revalidation.

operational_limits.statement: One reconciliation run uses one exact assessment and one Nucleus attempt with a closed basis grammar; there is no force path around stale bases and no automatic implementation transition.
No design-size, clause-count, reconciliation latency, or model-quality service-level objective is promised beyond the documented structural checks.

compatibility_and_evolution.statement: Capability contract version 1 preserves dN and aN bindings, immutable predecessor and correction history, the closed basis grammar, nine clause kinds, and versioned Nucleus toolsets and schemas.
No deprecation period, cross-version design migration protocol, or external-system compatibility window is promised.

reliances.statement: Proposal and correction rely on Nucleus for one constrained model execution, authentication, durable job state, and raw protocol history; Todo remains authoritative for design records and all decisions.
